<a id="aliens_counting"></a>
## Synth-Rock: `aliens_counting.yml`

A mid-eighties synth-rock anthem in the manner of The Final Countdown, on that song's chords in
another key, with a fanfare of its own in sixteenths on synth brass. A Guitarify makes the guitar's
held notes power chords, ringing under the fanfare and a muted gallop in the verse.

<a id="annandale"></a>
## Jazz-Rock: `annandale.yml`

A seventies jazz-rock song in the manner of Steely Dan's My Old School, with a horn line of its own.
A straight groove under a pumping piano on chords with added ninths; the guitar answers each line of
the verse; horns punch the chorus, which is sung high in harmony, and play a riff on I bVII IV
between sections; a guitar solo over the verse.

<a id="bad_pelican"></a>
## Galloping Heavy Metal Epic: `bad_pelican.yml`

A galloping heavy metal epic of the mid eighties in the manner of Rime of the Ancient Mariner (Iron
Maiden), with riffs and tunes of its own. A bass and guitars galloping on i VI VII; a narrating
verse and a broad chorus; twin guitars in thirds; a middle at 80 for a bass alone, a clean guitar
and a pad; a build on tom-toms into a fast instrumental at 168; the chorus again at the gallop.

<a id="gain_distance_pedestrian"></a>
## Funky Hard Rock: `gain_distance_pedestrian.yml`

A funky hard rock song of the early seventies in the manner of Walk Away (James Gang), with a riff
and tunes of its own. A syncopated riff of single notes and rests on an overdriven guitar against a
funky kit with ghost notes; a bluesy verse over the riff; a chorus in harmony on IV, I and V; a
solo; a long ending of two slide guitars on flat VII, IV and I.

<a id="green_men"></a>
## Pop-Punk Strumming: `green_men.yml`

A fast pop-punk song in the manner of American Idiot (Green Day): a stop-start riff of power chords,
and wide open choruses. A riff of power chords, two to a bar, I IV bVII IV; a verse muted for two
bars and answered for two; a chorus on IV I V I; a solo over the chorus chords.

<a id="know_your_slang"></a>
## Indie Rock: `know_your_slang.yml`

An upbeat indie rock song in two moods after the Shins' New Slang and Know Your Onion: a bass-and-
strum acoustic guitar with a tambourine, then a jangling electric guitar at a faster tempo. A bass
note and a strum to each chord, a tambourine in eighths and a busy bass; the second half faster and
jangling, with a chorus of its own.

<a id="loud_complaint"></a>
## Fast Heavy Metal: `loud_complaint.yml`

A fast British heavy metal song of the early eighties in the manner of Screaming for Vengeance
(Judas Priest), with riffs and tunes of its own. A riff for two guitars a third apart over a kick in
constant eighths; a clipped verse on i VI VII; a chorus of long high notes on i VI III VII; a twin-
guitar tune, a solo from each guitar and a breakdown.

<a id="not_werewolves"></a>
## Outlaw Piano Rock: `not_werewolves.yml`

An upbeat honky-tonk piano rock song of outlaws on the chords of Warren Zevon's Frank and Jesse
James, opening like saloon music. The piano is the star: a stride left hand, a bass note and a chord
for each chord of the song, moved by a Progression and voiced by Voice leading, under a ragtime
right hand; the verse two chords a bar on vi I, V I, vi V, IV I; a ballad in the middle; ends on vi.

<a id="spot_over_there"></a>
## Power-Pop: `spot_over_there.yml`

An early 2000s power-pop song in the manner of Stacy's Mom (Fountains of Wayne): muted power chords
in the verse, open chords in the chorus, and a key change for the solo. A muted verse on I IV V IV,
two chords a bar; a pre-chorus on iii IV; a chorus on IV I V vi; the solo and last chorus a minor
third higher.

<a id="training_montage"></a>
## Arena-Rock: `training_montage.yml`

An early-eighties film anthem in the manner of Eye of the Tiger, on that song's verse and chorus
chords in another key, for a training montage: a Guitarify plays muted power-chord stabs with the
kick, then down strokes and a chug under a driving rock beat and a brass lead. The rhythm and the
melody are its own.

<a id="volcano"></a>
## Guitar Showpiece: `volcano.yml`

A solo guitar showpiece of a minute and a half in the manner of Van Halen's Eruption: the band hits a
chord and leaves the guitar alone for picked runs, a dive, tremolo picking that a Drift moves about,
a fast study a Progression takes round the circle of fifths, and tapped arpeggios, a triad broken up
by an arpeggiator in sixteenth-note triplets. No episode comes back, and each has a tempo of its own.

<a id="why_say_it_again"></a>
## New Wave: `why_say_it_again.yml`

A taut new wave song of the late seventies in the manner of Psycho Killer (Talking Heads), with a
bass line and tunes of its own. A staccato bass alone, then a plain kit and two thin guitars; a
clipped verse on a dominant I and a flat VII; a stuttering chorus on flat VI, flat VII and a minor
i; a bridge of long notes; a coda of scratching guitar.
